name: APT10
affiliation_detail:
Associated to Huaying Haitai Science and Technology Development Company, based in Tianjin, China by both U.S. DOJ indictment (2018) and Intrusion Truth (2018). According to the writings, operators acted in association with the Chinese Ministry of State Security's (MSS) Tianjin State Security Bureau. 
Two members were indicted: Zhu Hua (aliases: Afwar, CVNX, Alayos, Godkiller) — a penetration tester who engaged in hacking and recruited members; and Zhang Shilong (aliases: Baobeilong, Zhang Jianguo, Atreexp) — who developed and tested malware. Both worked for Huaying Haitai in Tianjin.
entity_name: Huaying Haitai Science and Technology Development Co., Ltd.
description:
APT10 is a Chinese state-sponsored cyber espionage group affiliated with the MSS's Tianjin State Security Bureau, operating through the front company Huaying Haitai. 
Active since at least 2006, (U.S. DOJ, 2018) APT10 initially focused on the U.S. defense industrial base and Japanese organizations (FireEye/Mandiant, 2017) before expanding its scope with Operation Cloud Hopper, a supply-chain campaign targeting managed IT service providers (MSPs) worldwide to gain access to their clients' networks. (PwC & BAE, 2017)
This MSP compromise gave APT10 access to intellectual property across dozens of industries in at least a dozen countries. The group has also conducted extensive direct targeting of Japanese private and government organizations. (PwC & BAE, 2017) 
Two members (Zhu Hua and Zhang Shilong) were indicted by the DOJ in December 2018, and the group was sanctioned by the EU in 2020. Despite these actions, APT10 appears to have continued operations, with Symantec (2022) documenting global espionage campaigns as recently as 2022 using updated tooling including the SodaMaster backdoor, and Kaspersky (2022) associating APT10 with 2022 LODEINFO malware campaign targeting Japanese government orgs.

campaigns.name: Operation Cloud Hopper (MSP targeting)
campaigns.description: APT10's most significant campaign, targeting managed IT service providers (MSPs) worldwide as a supply-chain attack vector to reach their clients' networks. PwC and BAE Systems jointly reported the campaign in April 2017. APT10 compromised MSPs by exploiting their trusted network access and legitimate credentials (often with domain admin privileges) to "hop" into client networks across dozens of industries. Victims included major global MSPs (including HPE, IBM, and others per Reuters reporting), with affected organizations in the UK, US, Japan, India, Canada, Brazil, France, Norway, Finland, Switzerland, South Africa, and Australia. The UK NCSC issued an advisory urging organizations to demand evidence from their MSPs. A 2019 Reuters investigation revealed the campaign was significantly larger than initially reported, with HPE fighting the attackers for at least five years.

campaigns.name: Japanese organizations targeting campaign
campaigns.description: APT10 has maintained a persistent focus on Japanese organizations throughout its operational history. This includes targeting of Japanese academic and industrial entities (documented by Palo Alto Unit 42 in 2017), Japanese corporations with the UPPERCUT/ANEL and SNUGRIDE backdoors (FireEye 2018), and Japanese firms and their subsidiaries in 17 locations exploiting the Zerologon vulnerability (Symantec 2020). APT10's Japanese targeting has used dedicated malware families (ChChes) and C2 domains spoofing legitimate Japanese organizations.

campaigns.name: U.S. government and Navy data theft (DOJ Indictment)
campaigns.description: Per the DOJ indictment, APT10 conducted intrusions against at least 45 technology companies and U.S. government agencies over 12 years, stealing intellectual property, confidential business data, and personally identifiable information (PII) of more than 100,000 U.S. Navy personnel including social security numbers, dates of birth, and salary information. Targeted industries included aviation, satellite technology, pharmaceutical, computer processor, automotive, oil and gas exploration, and manufacturing. The group also compromised NASA, JPL, and the U.S. Attorney's Office in SDNY.

campaigns.name: Global espionage expansion (Cicada 2021-2022)
campaigns.description: Symantec documented APT10/Cicada targeting government, legal, religious, and NGO entities across the U.S., Canada, Hong Kong, Turkey, Israel, India, Montenegro, and Italy. The group exploited unpatched Microsoft Exchange Server vulnerabilities for initial access and deployed the SodaMaster backdoor and a custom loader via VLC Media Player DLL side-loading. Attackers maintained persistence on some networks for up to nine months. This campaign represented a significant broadening of APT10's target scope beyond its traditional Japanese focus.
